scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: An MRI sees inside your body in fine detail, without any X rays. So how does it see?

scenes.name: magnet
scenes.text: The tube is a huge magnet, around one point five to three tesla. Tens of thousands of times stronger than Earth's magnetic field.

scenes.name: align
scenes.text: Your body is full of water, and water has hydrogen. Their nuclei act like tiny magnets, and line up with the field.

scenes.name: pulse
scenes.text: A radio pulse knocks them out of line. When it stops, they relax back, giving off faint radio signals.

scenes.name: where
scenes.text: Extra coils make the field slightly different at each spot, so each signal reveals its location. That loud knocking is those coils switching.

scenes.name: image
scenes.text: Fat, water and other tissues relax at different speeds, so a computer turns the signals into a detailed image.

scenes.name: safe
scenes.text: No ionising radiation is used. But the magnet is always on, so metal objects are strictly kept out.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Magnet, hydrogen, radio, image. Seeing with physics. Follow for more on how things really work.
